selection_process: Stage Details
Stage I – English Typing Test (Qualifying) 10 minutes; minimum speed 40 w.p.m.; permissible mistakes 3% of total words typed (characters-with-space method)

Stage II – English Shorthand Test 110 w.p.m.; 550-word passage dictated in 5 minutes; 45 minutes for transcription; 120 marks; permissible mistakes 5% (27.5 mistakes); 4 marks deducted per full mistake, 2 marks per half mistake; more than 27.5 mistakes disqualifies; best of two attempts considered

Stage III – Main (Descriptive) Examination 100 marks; 120 minutes; Essay (250 words, 40 marks), Letter Writing (15 marks), Grammar & Comprehension (25 marks), Translation Hindi-English & English-Hindi (10+10 marks); passing marks 50% for General, 45% for Reserved/PwBD categories
Stage IV – Interview 15 marks; no minimum qualifying marks

how_to_apply: Register for online application using your email ID and mobile number; note the system-generated registration/application number.
Fill up the application form online by visiting www.delhihighcourt.nic.in.
Upload a scanned colour passport-size photograph in JPEG format (100 KB to 200 KB, not more than three months old, with 3/4th face coverage).
Capture and upload a live photograph via webcam/mobile device, matching the uploaded passport photo.
Upload left-hand thumb impression in JPEG format (50 KB to 200 KB); right-hand thumb impression may be used if left is unavailable.
Upload scanned signature in JPEG format (50 KB to 150 KB) – illegible or capital-letter signatures will be rejected.
Pay the prescribed fee online via UPI, Net Banking, Credit Card, or Debit Card.
Generate and save the Confirmation Page after successful fee payment – submission is complete only when this page is generated.

Use the correction window (12.10.2026 to 14.10.2026) if needed to modify any details except Name, Category, Date of Birth, and Mobile Number; corrections can be made up to two times, with charges of Rs. 200/- for the first correction and Rs. 500/- for the second.
important_instructions: No offline application will be accepted or entertained. Applications received without the prescribed fee will be summarily rejected; no representation against such rejection will be entertained. The medium of examination shall be English language only. Candidates must write their name, date of birth, and parent's/spouse's name strictly as per the matriculation certificate. At every stage of examination, candidates must carry two passport-size colour photographs (as uploaded) and one original photo ID proof (Aadhaar, Driving Licence, Voter ID, PAN Card, University/College/Government ID, Employer ID, ESM Discharge Book, or similar). No scrutiny of eligibility is done before the Document Verification/Interview stage; candidature remains provisional until then. Candidates must disclose any pending criminal proceedings or FIRs in the application form; concealment may lead to disqualification. The Delhi High Court reserves the right to alter the number of vacancies, modify the examination process, and fix minimum cut-off marks without assigning any reason. No TA/DA will be paid for appearing in the Typing Test, Shorthand Test, Written Test, or Interview. Selected candidates should be prepared to work at odd hours and on holidays, if required. No re-evaluation or re-checking of scores at any stage is permitted. The examination schedule indicated in the notice is tentative; changes will be communicated only through the official website.

content_sections.heading: Delhi High Court SPA & PA Vacancy 2026 – Post Details
content_sections.text: A total of 150 posts are being filled – 117 Senior Personal Assistant and 33 Personal Assistant, both Group 'B' posts. Category-wise vacancy breakups are given below. Since there is no vacancy under the General category for the post of Personal Assistant, all clauses in the notice pertaining to the General category apply only to the Senior Personal Assistant post. Within the total vacancies, posts are also reserved horizontally for Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD) – 7 posts out of 117 SPA vacancies, and 3 posts out of 33 PA vacancies. The disability-wise breakup is given below.

content_sections.heading: Delhi High Court SPA & PA Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Applicants must be citizens of India or subjects of Nepal, as per instructions issued by the Government of India from time to time. Nepal subjects must hold a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government of India; an offer of appointment will be given only after this certificate is produced. Candidates already in Government service must intimate their Department/Office and produce a No Objection Certificate at the stage of Document Verification/Interview if successful. Check Delhi High Court Personal Assistant Syllabus 2026

content_sections.heading: Delhi High Court SPA & PA Qualification
content_sections.text: All educational qualifications must be from a University/Institution/Board recognised by the Government of India or approved by Government regulatory bodies, with the final result declared on or before the closing date for receipt of online applications. Candidates must submit a separate application for each post (SPA and PA) along with the requisite fee for each.

rows.educational_qualification_as_on_05_10_20: Graduate from a recognised University with speed of not less than 110 w.p.m. in Shorthand (English) and 40 w.p.m. in Typewriting (English) on Computer, with good working knowledge of Computer
Graduate from a recognised University with speed of not less than 100 w.p.m. in Shorthand (English) and 40 w.p.m. in Typewriting (English) on Computer, with good working knowledge of Computer

content_sections.heading: Delhi High Court SPA & PA Age Limit
content_sections.text: As on 01.01.2026, a candidate's age should not be below 18 years and not over 32 years (born not earlier than 02.01.1994 and not later than 01.01.2008). Date of birth as recorded in the Matriculation/Secondary Examination Certificate or an equivalent certificate alone will be accepted; no subsequent request for change will be entertained. PwBD relaxation applies only to candidates with benchmark disability of 40% or more, in the specific disability categories for which vacancies have been reserved. Widows, divorcees, and certain other categories of married women get relaxation up to 40 years, as per Government of Delhi instructions dated 23.04.1984. There is no upper age limit for persons already in regular service in the Delhi High Court, subject to fulfilling the educational qualification – this relaxation does not apply to candidates working in other Government departments, PSUs, or Delhi District Courts. Candidates should ensure that they fulfill the prescribed age criteria. Calculate your exact age using our Age Calculator before submitting your application to confirm your eligibility.

rows.age_relaxation_beyond_upper_limit: 3 years (after deducting military service rendered); Disabled Defence Services personnel get relaxation up to 45 years, or 50 years for SC/ST

content_sections.heading: Delhi High Court SPA & PA Reservation
content_sections.text: 15% posts for Scheduled Castes, 7.5% for Scheduled Tribes, 27% for OBC (Non-Creamy Layer), 10% for EWS, and 4% for PwBD on horizontal basis, subject to availability and orders of the Chief Justice. There is no reservation for Ex-servicemen in Group 'A' & 'B' posts. Candidates must possess valid category certificates issued by the competent authority on or before the cut-off date of 05.10.2026; otherwise their claim for reserved category will not be entertained and the application will be considered under Unreserved category, if eligible. OBC candidates must hold a certificate issued by the competent authority of the Govt. of NCT of Delhi for castes recognised as OBC in Delhi; certificates for castes recognised only by the Government of India (for central posts) are not valid for this recruitment. A Non-Creamy Layer certificate issued in FY 2026-27 (01.04.2026 to 31.03.2027) is also required for OBC candidates. EWS reservation requires an Income and Asset Certificate in the prescribed format, valid as on the last date of application submission. Category or category code, once selected online, cannot be changed at any later stage. Candidature remains provisional until certificates are verified; fraudulent claims of SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwBD/ESM status will lead to debarment from the examination and legal action.

Applications without the prescribed fee will be summarily rejected. Separate fee is payable for each post (SPA and PA) applied for.

content_sections.heading: Delhi High Court SPA & PA Selection Process
content_sections.text: Both posts follow a four-stage selection process – English Typing Test, English Shorthand Test, Main (Descriptive) Examination, and Interview. The final merit list is prepared by adding marks from Stage II, III, and IV; Stage I (Typing Test) is qualifying only. Ties are resolved in order: Stage II marks, then Stage III marks, then Stage IV marks, then date of birth (older candidate preferred). No exemption from any stage, including Typing and Shorthand tests, is given to any candidate, including PwBD candidates; there is no provision for a scribe or compensatory time for PwBD candidates in this recruitment.

faq.question: Q1. What is Delhi High Court SPA & PA Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It is a recruitment examination conducted by the High Court of Delhi to fill 117 Senior Personal Assistant and 33 Personal Assistant posts, and to prepare a panel for future vacancies.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available in Delhi High Court SPA & PA Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There are 150 vacancies in total – 117 for Senior Personal Assistant and 33 for Personal Assistant.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification required for these posts?
faq.answer: A graduate degree from a recognised university, with English shorthand speed of 110 w.p.m. for SPA or 100 w.p.m. for PA, and typing speed of 40 w.p.m. on computer for both posts.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for Delhi High Court SPA & PA Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates must be between 18 and 32 years as on 01.01.2026, with age relaxation available for SC/ST, OBC-NCL, PwBD, and Ex-servicemen categories as per the notification.

faq.question: Q5. What is the last date to apply for Delhi High Court SPA & PA Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The last date for receipt of online applications and fee payment is 5 October 2026 (2300 hours). Applications open from 15 September 2026.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee for Delhi High Court SPA & PA Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Rs. 1,500 for General/OBC-NCL/EWS candidates and Rs. 1,300 for SC/ST/PwBD candidates, plus applicable transaction charges.

faq.question: Q7. What is the selection process for Delhi High Court SPA & PA Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: A four-stage process: English Typing Test (qualifying), English Shorthand Test, Main (Descriptive) Examination, and Interview. The final merit list is based on marks from the Shorthand Test, Main Examination, and Interview combined.

faq.question: Q8. How can I apply for Delhi High Court SPA & PA Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Applications must be submitted online through www.delhihighcourt.nic.in; no offline applications are accepted. Separate applications and fees are required for SPA and PA.

faq.question: Q9. Is there a correction window for the application form?
faq.answer: Yes, from 12 October 2026 to 14 October 2026, candidates can correct application details except Name, Category, Date of Birth, and Mobile Number, subject to correction charges of Rs. 200 (first time) and Rs. 500 (second time).

faq.question: Q10. Are PwBD candidates given any exemption from the shorthand or typing tests?
faq.answer: No. All candidates, including those in the PwBD category, must qualify every stage of the examination, including the Typing and Shorthand Tests; no scribe or compensatory time is provided.
